root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence centers on a structure that covers or encloses something, especially a canopy, tent, or surrounding barrier.
root_idea.development: The noun is described as an Arabicized Persian loanword. Its attested extensions move from physical canopies and tent enclosures to surrounding dust or smoke, including the Qur'anic fiery enclosure.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested nominal with a distinct lexical headword normalized to the classical citation form سُرَادِق.

senses.definition: The enclosing barrier of Hell surrounding its inhabitants.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Qur'anic possessive expression سُرَادِقُهَا, it is interpreted as a tent-like enclosure or as the wall or surrounding barrier of the fire.

senses.definition: The smoke of Hell rising and surrounding its inhabitants.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative Quran-attested interpretation of the same expression, focusing on the fire's enveloping smoke rather than a solid enclosure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A canopy, tent covering, or fabric enclosure around a court, tent, or other structure; by extension, a surrounding wall or enclosure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The enclosure may be roofed or unroofed. The word can also be used tropically of a canopy extended over something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dust rising, spreading, or diffusing itself.
Smoke rising high and surrounding a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the general Classical Arabic lexical use; the specifically Hell-related application is recorded separately under the Quranic form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A house or tent furnished with a سُرَادِق.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is also described as having its upper and lower parts fastened, curtained, or closed; the precise interpretation of this description is reported variably.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The physical canopy, tent, and enclosing-wall branch is represented together.
The general surrounding-smoke use is represented.
The Quranic enclosure, wall, and smoke interpretations are represented under the attested form.
The derived adjective and its house-or-tent construction are represented separately.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is a single possessive form, and the lexical interpretation allows both an enclosing wall or tent-like barrier and enveloping fire-smoke; these are kept as separate senses to preserve the attested interpretive distinction.
